requirements.evidence: Migrations match the spec exactly: `entities_slug_unique`, soft deletes, cascading FKs, `owner_seq` storedAs CASE plus `entity_memberships_one_owner` (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-26). The contract models, enum `manageable()`, factories with states, both policies, routes under `e/{entity:slug}` (routes/web.php:26-31), pick with Gate + audit + redirect (EntityController.php:13-25), mount-time authorization in all three components, owner-only settings link and notice (dashboard.blade.php:5-13), addMember duplicate checks on `email` (Members.php:46), assignRole Rule::in manageable roles (Members.php:70-72), last-manager guard (Members.php:97-104), Locked entity, delete clears session (Settings.php:70-88), and transfer demotes and then promotes in a transaction with lockForUpdate, returning 403 when the owner row is missing (Settings.php:90-122). Lang keys are present in both locales and docs/database-schema.md is updated.

conventions.evidence: Authorization goes through policies via Gate::authorize, `#[Fillable]` is set on both models, Blade components `<x-form-field>`/`<x-button>` are reused, Bulma markup is used, and CHANGELOG plus database-schema docs are updated. Deviations: every domain write (add member, assign role, remove member, save/delete/transfer entity) is coded inline in the Livewire components instead of `app/Actions/*` classes (Members.php:36-118, Settings.php:39-122). Livewire validation uses inline `$this->validate([...])` arrays instead of the project's `#[Validate]` attributes (Members.php:40, Settings.php:43). Migration names `2026_08_01_000000/000001` suggest hand-written files rather than generated ones.

security.evidence: `#[Locked] public Entity $entity` is on all components. Every public action re-authorizes server-side (Members.php:38,68,93; Settings.php:41,72,92). Client IDs are resolved and scoped to the bound entity (`findMembership` abort_unless entity_id match, Members.php:139-145; transfer scopes `->admin()->whereKeyNot($owner->id)` on `$this->entity->memberships()`). All output uses `{{ }}`. Gaps with limited impact: public `$targetMembershipId` is untyped and has no `#[Validate]` rule, only an ad-hoc ctype_digit check (Settings.php:26,94). Destructive actions (delete, transfer, removeMember) have no rate limiting.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/EntityTest.php covers DB constraints (second owner, duplicate membership), both policies, pick success/403 with session untouched, auth+verified, the owner-only link and notice in both locales, 403 for non-members, add/duplicate/unknown email, employee 403 on add/assign, role validation including `owner`, remove rules including foreign membership and last manager, self-leave, settings save/slug uniqueness, the entity-swap tamper test, delete, and transfer happy path plus garbage targets. Gaps: the 'owner row vanished' test is stopped by the top-level `manageSettings` Gate before it reaches the in-transaction check, so Settings.php:97 is not exercised. assignRole with a membership of another entity (tamper) is not tested. There is no unauthorized-call test for save/delete beyond the mount check.

simplicity.evidence: The code is direct and does not add service layers. Small duplication: an identical `isManager` helper appears in both policies (EntityPolicy.php:37-40, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:29-32), and the session-clear-if-current snippet is repeated (Members.php:115-117, Settings.php:84-86). The `saved` flag and the slug-change redirect are reasonable additions.

readability.evidence: Methods are short and well named, and a few comments explain non-obvious choices ('Demote first: the unique owner index allows only one owner at any moment', Settings.php:107; 'The owner's role only changes through ownership transfer', Members.php:74). Sibling style is consistent (Layout attribute, typed returns). No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task. Out-of-scope items are not built: no onboarding, switcher, session-guard middleware, locale middleware or navbar changes. The extra audit log lines on member and settings writes and the validation attribute names in lang/pt_BR/validation.php:200-201 are small and support the feature.

issues.explanation: Domain writes (add/assign/remove member, update/delete entity, transfer ownership) are coded inline in Livewire components instead of one `app/Actions/*` class per use case, which the conventions require.
Validation uses inline rule arrays in `$this->validate([...])` rather than the project's `#[Validate]` attribute pattern on public properties.
Public `$targetMembershipId` is untyped and has no `#[Validate]` rule; it relies on an ad-hoc ctype_digit/abort check instead of declared validation.
Sensitive destructive actions (delete entity, transfer ownership, remove member) are not rate-limited, contrary to Livewire policy rule 9.
The 'owner row vanished' test is stopped by the top-level manageSettings Gate, so the in-transaction `$owner === null` guard in Settings::transfer is never exercised.
No tamper test calls assignRole with a membership ID from another entity, and save/delete have no unauthorized-call tests beyond the mount-level check.
Round synthetic timestamps suggest the migrations were hand-written rather than created with `make:migration`.
The same `isManager` role check is duplicated in both policies, and the session-clear snippet is duplicated in Members and Settings.

review.summary: The change implements the entities data model with a portable DB-enforced single owner, both policies, entity.pick, and the dashboard, members and settings Livewire pages with locked entities, per-action server-side authorization, scoped ID resolution and an atomic ownership transfer, backed by a broad Pest suite. Functionally it meets the task and is secure. However, it bypasses the project's Actions pattern for domain writes and its #[Validate] convention, and it leaves small gaps in validation, rate limiting and tamper tests, so I would approve it with requested follow-ups.
